title: Build the Eneo module kit
description:
Build the starter for Eneo modules: a FastAPI BFF package with the module contract, a React + Astryx UI package, and
a template app that new modules copy.

## Read first
- `README.md`, `docs/design.md`, `docs/plans/2026-10-01-module-kit-plan.md`.

## Scope
This repository only. Code is copied from `eneo-ai/eneo-mod-speech-to-text` at commit `f81a7dd`; that repository is
never changed from here.

## Order
Phase 0 → Phase 1 (BFF) and Phase 2 (UI, first part) → Phase 3 (template) → Phase 4 (session client, after
speech-to-text's Phase 1) → Phase 5 (integration and release). `br ready --json` gives the next bead.

## Success Criteria
- A module copied from `template/` signs in through Eneo's handoff, calls Eneo through the deny-by-default proxy and
  runs as one container on port 3001.
- Both packages are released as 0.1.0 and install into a clean consumer.
- No speech-to-text feature, route or copy is in the packages.

## Scope
Branch `feat/ui`.

Files: everything under `packages/ui/` except `src/session/` and `astryx.integration.mjs`; a `ui` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

Sources: `docs/reference/astryx-phase0-reference.patch` (theme, providers, jsdom shim), the `ModuleShell` code in the plan, and `frontend/components/Brand.tsx` in the speech-to-text clone.

## Out of scope
- Session screens, the Astryx integration manifest, a router, next-themes, an inline script, a cookie for the colour mode.
- Changing the theme's values: copy `eneo.theme.ts` unchanged.
- The speech-to-text repository: read it, never change it.
- Anything on the plan's "out of the kit entirely" list: the live transcription relay, artifact download naming,
  `/api/config`, the access-code login, any Eneo route in the kit's own allowlist.
- Next.js, Tailwind, Hono, a second UI library, an ejected Astryx component, authored StyleX.
- New runtime dependencies, and changes to the pinned versions.
- Work that belongs to another bead. If something outside this scope looks wrong, comment on this bead

1. Kickoff, before any code: read the card and its sources, write this phase's task list in the form of Phase 1's
   tasks (files, interfaces, changes from the source, test-first steps) as a comment on this bead, and get it reviewed.
2. Carry out the tasks (theme, colour mode, providers, shell, brand). One commit per task.
3. Run the card's exit checks. Open the pull request to `main` when the owner asks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `npm run -w packages/ui build` emits `dist/` and its tests pass.
- The built theme is committed in its own folder and CI fails when it is stale.
- The stored colour mode (`localStorage["theme"]`: `light`, `dark`, `system`) is applied on the first render; `system` follows the media query.
- The shell has one main region, a named navigation landmark and the Swedish skip link.
- `Brand` takes the product name as a prop and shows it alone until `/api/branding` has answered.
- The package imports nothing from a router, Next.js or the template.

## Verify
```bash
npm install && npm run -w packages/ui build && npm test -w packages/ui
```

title: Phase 1.9: a module's own routes are not shadowed by the proxy or the page fallback
description:
Found by the Phase 1 implementer (kit-bff) and reproduced: a route a module adds after `create_app(...)` is shadowed.
- Under `/api/eneo/`, the proxy catch-all swallows it (`POST /api/eneo/things/1/files` answers 403 "Eneo resource is not exposed").
- With `static_dir` set, the SPA fallback `GET /{path:path}` swallows a module's GET route (`GET /api/mine` answers 404), while a POST at the same path works.
- `/api` itself (no trailing slash) is served as the SPA page; the fallback only checks `startswith("api/")`.
`deps.py` already says a module declares its routes on a router before an app exists, but `create_app` has no way to take one, and `app.include_router(...)` afterwards has the ordering problem above. The template (Phase 3) and speech-to-text's own upload and audio routes (under `/api/eneo/...`) will hit this.

## Read first
- `docs/plans/2026-10-01-module-kit-plan.md`: Global Constraints, "How to work", Phase 1 Tasks 1.4, 1.5, 1.7.
- `docs/design.md`: K6, K7, K8, section 5.
- `AGENTS.md`.

## Scope
Branch `feat/bff` (continue it; one more commit). Files: `packages/bff/src/eneo_module_bff/app.py`, `web.py`, `packages/bff/tests/test_app.py`, `test_proxy.py`, `test_web.py`, `packages/bff/README.md`, `docs/design.md` (K7 and section 5), `docs/plans/2026-10-01-module-kit-plan.md` (the Task 1.4 interface block and the Phase 3 template row: say `routers=`).

The change, and only this:
1. `create_app(..., routers: Sequence[APIRouter] = ())`. Order of registration: auth router, health, branding, **the module's routers**, then the proxy router, then the static app last. A module's routes therefore win over the proxy catch-all and the SPA fallback; the module still declares its own `Depends(require_session)` and `Depends(require_same_origin)`.
2. The SPA fallback treats `api` and `api/...` as API: 404 JSON, never HTML.
3. A module router must not be able to turn the kit's own routes off: its routes are registered after them, so a duplicate of an kit route (`/api/auth/status`, `/health`, ...) does not replace it. Add a test that proves the kit's route still answers.

## Out of scope
- Any second mechanism (a 404-handler fallback, a plugin system, route priorities). One parameter, one order.
- Changing the proxy rules, `forward_upload`, `stream_signed`, the session code.
- Anything outside the files above.

## Steps
1. Write failing tests first (in the files above): a module router with `POST /api/eneo/things/{id}/files` and with `GET /api/mine` both answer (also with `static_dir` set); an unknown `/api/nope` and `/api` are 404 JSON; the kit's own `/api/auth/status` and `/health` are not replaced by a module router that declares them; the proxy still denies by default.
2. Run: they fail for the reasons above.
3. Implement the three points. Run the whole suite.
4. Update the docs listed in Scope. Commit: `feat(bff): a module's own routes go through create_app and win over the proxy and the page fallback`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The whole suite passes (112 existing + the new tests).
- `GET /api/mine` and `POST /api/eneo/things/1/files` declared on a module router answer, with and without `static_dir`.
- `/api` and `/api/anything-unknown` are 404 with a JSON body.
- The two exit greps (`access_code|AUTH_MODE|DEMO_SPACE|flows/`, and import-time state) still print nothing.

## Verify
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s packages/bff/tests -t packages/bff
```

## If blocked
Stop and comment on this bead. Do not work around the ordering.

## Steps to Reproduce
On `feat/bff` at 574cbca: `app = create_app(settings, static_dir=dist)`; `app.add_api_route("/api/mine", handler, methods=["GET"])` → `GET /api/mine` is 404 `{"detail":"Not Found"}`; `GET /api` returns the page.

title: Phase 1.10: security floors for the dependencies, tested at the floors and the newest, with a Python audit in CI
description:
The plan's Global Constraints pin the BFF package's dependencies "exactly equal to speech-to-text's": `fastapi==0.115.0`, `python-multipart==0.0.12`, which resolve Starlette 0.38.6. `pip-audit` reports 14 known vulnerabilities in those two packages (found 2026-10-01; see below). A new starter must not begin with them, and an exact-pinned library also forces every module that imports it to the same stack.

Evidence (lead's trial in throwaway virtualenvs, not in this repository): old pins → 14 advisories (python-multipart: multipart parser denial of service through preamble/epilogue/part headers CVE-2026-40347, CVE-2026-42561, excess logging CVE-2024-53981, negative Content-Length reads the body into memory CVE-2026-53540, urlencoded parser CVE-2026-53538/53539; Starlette: unbounded multipart field buffering CVE-2024-47874, event loop blocked on large upload roll-over CVE-2025-54121, unvalidated Host/path in request URL, form limits ignored for urlencoded CVE-2026-54283). Newest versions (fastapi 0.142.2, starlette 1.7.0, uvicorn 0.54.0, httpx 0.28.1, itsdangerous 2.2.0, python-multipart 0.0.32): `pip-audit` clean, and speech-to-text's 117 backend tests pass on them.
FastAPI reads a `File(...)` body before it runs a route's `Depends(...)`, so the multipart cost can be reached before the session check; the floors matter.

A library declares compatible ranges with security floors, not exact pins: `fastapi>=0.142.2,<1`, `starlette>=1.3.1,<2`, `uvicorn[standard]>=0.54,<1`, `httpx>=0.28,<1`, `itsdangerous>=2.2,<3`, `python-multipart>=0.0.31,<1`. 2. Change `pyproject.toml`; build two fresh venvs (floors, newest); run the suite in both; run `pip-audit` on both.

title: Phase 1.11: BFF hardening from the adversary review (header allowlist, control characters, set-cookie, inline files, callback input, config)
description:
The adversary review of the BFF (read-only agent, 2026-10-01, scripts reproduced each finding) found no exploitable P0, one P1 and several P2s. Everything below was verified by running it; the lead judged each item. Fixes are the clean, structural ones; items that are not fixed in code are fixed in the documents.

## Read first
- `docs/plans/2026-10-01-module-kit-plan.md`: Global Constraints, Phase 1 Tasks 1.2, 1.5, 1.6.
- `docs/design.md`: section 2 (contract), K6, K7.
- `AGENTS.md`.

## Scope
Branch `feat/bff` (continue it; after beads `.17` and `.18`). Files: `packages/bff/src/eneo_module_bff/{auth,proxy,transport,settings}.py`, their tests, `docs/design.md`, `docs/plans/2026-10-01-module-kit-plan.md`, `packages/bff/README.md`. One commit per numbered fix, tests first (each fix has a test that fails first, shown), then one `chore: update the Beads board` commit.

### Fix list
1. **P1 — only an allowlist of request headers reaches Eneo.** Today the proxy drops a denylist and forwards the rest, so `Transfer-Encoding`, `TE`, `Upgrade`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `X-Forwarded-*`, `Forwarded`, `X-Real-IP` reach Eneo on a pool shared by all users and carrying the service key (a chunked request arrives with both `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `Content-Length`; a user can forge `X-Forwarded-For`, which Eneo's audit log may record). Replace the denylist with `FORWARDED_REQUEST_HEADERS = {"accept", "accept-language", "content-type", "idempotency-key", "if-match", "if-none-match"}` (lowercase, exported constant) plus `create_app(..., forward_request_headers: Sequence[str] = ())` for a module that needs more; the credentials are still set by `upstream_auth_headers`. This deliberately departs from "copy the header sets unchanged" in plan Task 1.5: change that sentence and add one line in design K6 ("deny by default, for paths and for headers"). Tests: each header above is dropped; an allowlisted one passes; a module-added one passes; the custom API-key header name and `Cookie`/`Authorization`/`Origin`/`Referer` still never reach Eneo.
2. **P2 — a path with a control character or a backslash is refused (403), never 500.** `flows/a%00b/runs/` and `%0D` raise `httpx.InvalidURL` (not a `RequestError`), and a backslash goes upstream literally. Extend `leaves_route` to refuse any decoded character below U+0020, U+007F and `\`. Test the proxy and `forward_upload`/`stream_signed` ids.
3. **P2 — Eneo's `Set-Cookie` is not passed to the browser** (several were merged into one line, and a cookie named like the module's session would overwrite it). Add `set-cookie` to the response headers that are dropped. Proxy responses also get `Cache-Control: private, no-store` when Eneo sent none.
4. **P2 — a streamed file is shown inline only if it is safe to.** `stream_signed` asks Eneo for `inline` and forwards `Content-Type`, so a user-uploaded `text/html` file is served inline from the module's origin (only the CSP protects it). Force `Content-Disposition: attachment` unless the media type is `audio/*`, `video/*`, `application/pdf` or `image/png|jpeg|gif|webp`; keep `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Add `inline_types: Sequence[str]` to `stream_signed` to widen it. Test text/html → attachment, audio/webm with Range → inline and 206.
5. **P2 — callback input is handled, not crashed on.** A non-ASCII `state` with a valid cookie makes `secrets.compare_digest` raise `TypeError` (500): compare `.encode()`d bytes. A second login must end the session the browser already holds (delete the old session id from the store in `callback`): today a second login leaves two sessions alive.
6. **P2 — `next` is bounded and cannot swallow the query.** A 6 000-character `next` makes an 8 KB state cookie that browsers drop (login fails as `invalid_state`): `module_path` falls back to `home_path` above 512 characters. `with_query` must put the query before a `#` fragment (use `urlsplit`/`urlunsplit`); today `/page#top` becomes `/page#top?fel=annan-anvandare` and the UI never sees the signal.
7. **P2 — configuration is normalised.** `module_origin` and the `Origin` it is compared with are compared in canonical form (lowercase scheme and host, default port dropped): `https://Mod.Example.SE` or `:443` makes every write 403 today. A token's `session_expires_at` without a time zone is read as UTC (today as local time: a 2 h shift under `Europe/Stockholm`). `_required_url` refuses a bare `?` or `#` (`"?" in value or "#" in value`).
8. **P2 — an unexpected exception while refreshing does not turn into 500 on every request.** In `_refresh`, catch `Exception` (after the specific handling), log it, and treat it like "Eneo cannot answer": keep the token and retry later.

### Document fixes (no code)
- Design §2: "reject a missing, reused or mismatched state" → say what the code does: the state is bound to the browser by a signed, short-lived cookie that the callback deletes; one-time use is enforced by Eneo's ticket (do **not** build a seen-state store).
- Design §2: "On 401/403 end the session" → "on any refusal other than 408, 429 or 5xx".
- Plan Phase 3 "Backend test (Review Focus 5)": the route walker must cover WebSocket routes too (`APIWebSocketRoute` has no `.methods`): every WebSocket route needs both `require_session` and `require_same_origin`. Write that test against a router with one WebSocket route in this bead (`test_deps.py`) so Phase 3 can reuse it.

## Out of scope
- Request body size limits and unauthenticated body parsing (a separate bead from the performance review).
- A seen-state store, rate limiting, sticky or shared sessions.
- Anything in `web.py`, `app.py` beyond the `forward_request_headers` parameter.

## Steps to Reproduce
The adversary's scripts are under /tmp/adv/ (a8_te.py: chunked request reaches Eneo with Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length; a3_proxy.py, a7_transport.py: %00 gives 500 and a backslash goes upstream). Each fix's first test reproduces its finding.

## Steps
For each numbered fix: write the failing test(s), run them (show the failure), implement, run the whole suite, commit with message `fix(bff): <what>`. Then the documents. Then the Phase 1 exit again (suite at floors and newest after `.18`, the two greps, wheel build and install, suite against the wheel), re-close `.10`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every fix has a test that failed before and passes after; the whole suite passes.
- The adversary's reproduction scripts no longer reproduce items 1–8 (re-run `/tmp/adv/a*.py` if they still exist, otherwise the new tests are the proof).
- The two exit greps still print nothing.

## Verify
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s packages/bff/tests -t packages/bff
```

## If blocked
Stop and comment on this bead. Do not weaken a fix to keep a carried-over test passing; report the test.
close_reason: Eight fixes, one commit each on feat/bff, each with tests written first and shown failing, then the whole suite green (117 -> 155 tests). 1 P1 header allowlist 366a363: +5 tests; failed first on x-forwarded-for reaching Eneo and no ValueError for credential/framing names; FORWARDED_REQUEST_HEADERS + create_app(forward_request_headers=); a module cannot add Cookie/Authorization/Origin/Referer/X-API-Key/Host/Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding (ValueError), the configured API-key header stays the module's; plan Task 1.5 sentence and design K6 changed. 2 control chars/backslash c1187d9: +6; failed 200!=403 and 502!=403; leaves_route refuses <U+0020, U+007F and backslash in the decoded path and after a second decode; ordinary ids (space, non-ASCII, ~) still pass; NOTE a decoded newline is a 404 from the router's own {path:path} pattern (it does not match \n) before the proxy, not 403: never reaches Eneo, never 500, pinned by a test. 3 Set-Cookie + cache 0613b39: +2; failed with both cookies merged into one set-cookie line; set-cookie dropped, Cache-Control private,no-store when Eneo sent none (Eneo's value kept otherwise). 4 inline only if safe d4b565f: +6; failed with text/html forwarded inline; attachment (keeping Eneo's filename) unless audio/*, video/*, application/pdf, image/png|jpeg|gif|webp; stream_signed(inline_types=); nosniff set on the stream. 5 callback ea1eb5e: +4; failed TypeError on non-ASCII state and old session alive; bytes compare; callback deletes the held session after the new one exists (not on a failed login or renewal by another user). 6 next/with_query afb5954: +4; failed with a 6322-byte state cookie and /inloggad#top?fel=...; next above 512 characters falls back to home_path; with_query puts the query before the fragment. (The size test uses random characters: itsdangerous compresses a repeated one.) 7 configuration 689840c: +5; canonical_origin (lower-case scheme/host, default port dropped, strict for an Origin header: no path/query/userinfo); naive session_expires_at is UTC (tested under TZ=Europe/Stockholm); _required_url refuses bare ? and #. 8 refresh cede23d: +2; failed RuntimeError reaching every request; _refresh catches Exception (not BaseException), logs, keeps the token, retries in 10 s, one attempt shared by 8 concurrent requests. Walker de3d152: +4 in test_deps.py: unguarded_routes(*routers) checks require_session (however deep), require_same_origin for writes and every WebSocket route, and reports a route it cannot check. DISCOVERY: FastAPI 0.142 keeps an included router as one _IncludedRouter in app.routes, so a walker over app.routes cannot see module routes through public API; the walker therefore takes the module's routers (router.routes) and the plan's Phase 3 row now says so. Docs 9832aa8: design section 2 (state binding and one-time use by Eneo's ticket, refresh refusals other than 408/429/5xx, header allowlist, a new login ends the held session). Adversary scripts /tmp/adv re-run on the fixed code: a8 (real socket) Eneo gets Content-Length 5 and no Transfer-Encoding, browser gets no Set-Cookie; a7 %00/%5C -> 403 no upstream, text/html -> attachment; a1/a2/a9 non-ASCII state -> invalid_state, oversized next cookie 262-265 bytes, fel kept before #top, canonical origin, bare ?/# refused, naive time zone same under UTC and Stockholm, one session after two logins; a4 case 8: [200,200,200], one refresh attempt, session kept; a5 WebSocket and origin checks as before. a3's header section errors on a script bug (explicit Cookie header replaces the session cookie under Starlette 1.x). Both exit greps empty. Not in this bead's list, seen in the same scripts, NOT changed: Eneo's Location header still reaches the browser (internal host); a malformed signed-url answer from Eneo (not JSON, no url, odd expires_at) is a 500; a signed-URL cache entry outlives the logout until its expiry (keyed by session id, so unreachable without the cookie).

title: Phase 1.12: HTTP client — httpx2 or httpx, decided with evidence (Starlette deprecates the httpx test client)
description:
Newest Starlette warns on every test client: "Using `httpx` with `starlette.testclient` is deprecated; install `httpx2` instead." (observed 2026-10-01, Starlette 1.7.0). PyPI: `httpx2` 2.13.1, "The next generation HTTP client", repository `pydantic/httpx2`; `httpx` itself has no stable release after 0.28.1 (only 1.0.dev pre-releases). The BFF's runtime HTTP client is `httpx.AsyncClient` (callback, refresh, proxy, uploads, streaming), so this is a decision about the runtime dependency as well as the tests. The owner wants everything on the latest, maintained versions.

## Read first
- `packages/bff/src/eneo_module_bff/{app,auth,proxy,transport}.py` (every `httpx` use), `packages/bff/pyproject.toml`, `packages/bff/tests/`.
- `docs/design.md` section 6.
- `AGENTS.md`.

## Scope
Branch `feat/bff` (continue it; after beads `.19` and the performance bead if one is created). Files: `packages/bff/pyproject.toml`, `packages/bff/src/eneo_module_bff/*.py` (imports and the client class only), `packages/bff/tests/*`, `docs/design.md` (one paragraph recording the decision), the plan's Tech stack and pin lines.

## Out of scope
- Any behaviour change. Any new feature of the new client (HTTP/2, brotli, zstd) unless it is needed for parity.
- speech-to-text's backend (it keeps `httpx` until it adopts the kit or gets its own bead).

## Steps
1. Read the `httpx2` changelog and release history: how often it releases, who maintains it, open security advisories (`pip-audit`, GitHub security tab via `gh api repos/pydantic/httpx2`), and whether `httpcore2` is pinned to it exactly (`httpcore2==2.13.1`). Write the findings (five lines) as a comment on this bead.
2. Trial in a throwaway venv: replace `httpx` with `httpx2` in the package and tests (`import httpx2 as httpx` is NOT acceptable in the result: change the names properly), run the whole suite, then the adversary scripts that exist under `/tmp/adv/` for the proxy, uploads and streaming, and measure: upload of 300 MB and 1 GB to a slow fake Eneo, 20 concurrent Range streams, peak RSS and event-loop latency, the same numbers on `httpx` 0.28.1 (a script under `/tmp`, not committed).
3. Decide, with the numbers: use `httpx2` if the suite passes, memory and latency are no worse, and it is actively maintained with no open advisory; otherwise keep `httpx` for the runtime, switch only the tests' client if Starlette allows it, and record why. If the answer is not clear, stop and put the numbers and your recommendation on this bead for the lead.
4. If switching: update `pyproject.toml` floors (`httpx2>=<tested minimum>,<3`), CI matrix (floors and newest), `pip-audit`, docs. One commit: `refactor(bff): use httpx2, the maintained HTTP client`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The decision and its evidence are on the bead and in `docs/design.md`.
- If switched: no `import httpx` remains in the package or tests, the suite passes at the floors and the newest, `pip-audit` is clean, the Starlette deprecation warning is gone, and the measured memory and latency are no worse than with `httpx`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -W error::DeprecationWarning -m unittest discover -s packages/bff/tests -t packages/bff
```

Stop and comment on this bead with the numbers. Do not switch on a hunch.

title: Phase 1.13: Location header, malformed signed-URL answers, signed-URL cache tied to the session
description:
Three findings the Phase 1.11 hardening run saw in the adversary's scripts and did not change (reported by kit-bff, 2026-10-01). All are in the transport and proxy code.

## Read first
- `packages/bff/src/eneo_module_bff/{proxy,transport}.py` and their tests, `docs/design.md` K6, K7.
- `AGENTS.md`.

## Scope
Branch `feat/bff` (after beads `.20` and, if created, the performance bead). Files: `packages/bff/src/eneo_module_bff/{proxy,transport,auth}.py`, their tests, `docs/design.md` (one line each).
1. **Eneo's `Location` header reaches the browser** with Eneo's internal host (`ENEO_BACKEND_URL`), which the browser cannot reach and which leaks the internal topology. Drop `location` from proxied response headers (the module never follows redirects: `follow_redirects=False`), and make a 3xx from Eneo a 502 `upstream_redirect` JSON error, because no module route is expected to redirect. Test both.
2. **A malformed signed-URL answer from Eneo gives a 500** (`payload["url"]` missing or not a string, `expires_at` not a number). Treat any malformed mint answer as 502 `upstream_invalid` JSON, with the log line naming the mint path (not the body). Test: missing `url`, non-string `url`, non-numeric `expires_at`, non-JSON body, a `url` on a different scheme than http(s).
3. **A signed-URL cache entry outlives the session** (it is keyed by the session cookie value and holds a bearer URL to a file for up to 15 minutes). Evict a session's entries when the session ends: on logout, on expiry (`ModuleSessionStore` deletion), and when a refresh ends the session. The cache moves into the session store's lifetime (a field of the stored session or a store method), not a second dict that has to be kept in step. Test: logout drops the entries; expiry drops them; a different session's entries stay.

## Out of scope
- Cache size bounds, request body limits (the performance bead), anything in `web.py`.

## Steps to Reproduce
From the adversary's scripts under /tmp/adv (a Location header on an Eneo 3xx; a mint answer without a url; a logout followed by a stream from the same cache key); each item's first test reproduces it.

## Steps
Tests first (shown failing) per item; one commit per item; board export commit; re-run the Phase 1 exit once.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each item has a test that failed before and passes after; the whole suite passes at the floors and the newest; the two exit greps print nothing.
- `Location` never reaches the browser; a malformed mint answer is a 502, never 500; no signed-URL entry survives its session.

## Verify
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s packages/bff/tests -t packages/bff
```

## If blocked
Stop and comment on this bead.

title: Phase 1.14 (P0): cap the proxy body and never read a request body before auth
description:
Source: kit-perf review of feat/bff @ 5c53451 (real uvicorn + fake Eneo; Linux container re-runs). Two P0 memory/DoS findings.

## Problem
1. Proxy body is uncapped: `request.body()` (proxy.py ~161) plus `upstream.content` peak at ~2.07x the body: 50 MB -> +105 MB RSS, 500 MB -> +1035 MB. One authenticated 700 MB POST OOM-killed the BFF in a 768 MB container.
2. Bodies are read BEFORE `Depends(require_session)`: FastAPI parses a module route's JSON body / `File(...)` part before dependencies run. 200 MB JSON to a route with a body model: +814 MB RSS, 250 ms loop stall, then 401; 400 MB OOM-killed the container. A 300 MB multipart file part spooled ~300 MB to /tmp, then 401. No session needed.

## Required behaviour
- Proxy: read `request.stream()` with a running size; 413 above `Settings.proxy_max_body_bytes` (default 10 MiB); reject at once on a declared Content-Length above the cap; a body with no Content-Length (chunked) is counted while streaming and aborted at the cap. The response side stays as is (Eneo is trusted).
- Uploads: `forward_upload(request, path)` parses the multipart itself AFTER the module's own dependencies: no `File(...)` in a module's route. Content-Length required (411) and <= `Settings.max_upload_bytes` (413); `request.form(max_files=1, max_fields=0)`; a non-file field -> 400; aborted uploads leave no temp files or fds. Update the template/docs example that shows a module upload route.
- Other body-bearing requests (JSON etc.) must not make the BFF read or buffer an unbounded amount before auth. Choose the SMALLEST mechanism that is correct and document it; a pure-ASGI body cap (Content-Length and streamed count -> 413) on non-multipart bodies needs no session lookup and cannot break a module's deliberately public POST route (a session-cookie 401 gate would). If you pick the 401 gate instead, say how a public route opts out.
- Keep K6/K7: kit routes unchanged in contract, module declares its own Depends.

## Tests first (each proven failing before the fix)
- unauth 300 MB multipart -> 401 with the body unread (assert via receive-count or RSS/temp-dir probe, not timing); auth 300 MB under the cap -> 200; over cap -> 413; missing Content-Length -> 411; non-file field -> 400; 8 aborted uploads -> 0 leftover fds/temp files.
- JSON body over the cap, with and without Content-Length (chunked) -> 413 and bounded memory; proxy POST over the cap -> 413, under -> forwarded byte-identical.
- Existing 155+ tests still pass; httpx2 and floor/latest CI matrix unchanged.

## Acceptance
Measured RSS peak for a 500 MB authenticated proxy POST and a 400 MB unauthenticated JSON POST stays within a few MB of baseline (record the numbers). Adversary pass (kit-adversary) on the diff before close.
close_reason: Commits 0ef2d41 (the change) and db7eff5 (the adversary pass's findings) on feat/bff. Tests first and shown failing: the unauthenticated 64 MiB multipart taken in full before the 401, the unauthenticated JSON body taken in full and answered 422, the 64 MiB proxy POST buffered and forwarded with no cap (all reproduced on the old code with lazily fed bodies, nothing materialised); then each new test failing for the stated reason before its fix. 226 tests green at the floors (starlette 1.3.1) and the newest (-W error::DeprecationWarning). DESIGN, the smallest mechanism that is correct for non-multipart bodies and for the rest: ONE pure-ASGI BodyLimitMiddleware (limits.py) caps EVERY request body at Settings.max_body_bytes (10 MiB, env MAX_BODY_BYTES) for every route and content type: 413 at once when the declared length is above the ceiling, else as soon as the stream passes the cap, by raising HTTPException(413) from the wrapped receive (FastAPI turns any other exception raised while it reads a body into a 400). It looks at no session. WHY A MODULE'S DELIBERATELY PUBLIC POST ROUTE STILL WORKS: nothing in the middleware asks who the caller is, so a public route is capped like any other and still answers; a session-cookie 401 gate would have broken it (tested: small body 200 without a session, 400 MiB body 413 without a session). forward_upload(request, upstream_path) has no File(...) in the module's route: after the route's dependencies and its own checks (Content-Length required 411; at most Settings.max_upload_bytes 1 GiB, env MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES, 413) it sets request.scope['eneo_module_bff.body_limit'] and the middleware counts the bytes that arrive against that; then request.form(max_files=1, max_fields=0) inside async with, exactly one UploadFile named upload_file (else 400, and the parse stops at the first field: a text field in front of a big file leaves the file unread, tested), and no control character in the file name or part content type (400, never forwarded, never a 500). The bead's wording differs in three places on purpose: (1) the setting is max_body_bytes, not proxy_max_body_bytes, because it covers every body, not only the proxy's; (2) there is no separate read_body for the proxy: the proxy's request.body() is bounded by the middleware (I wrote read_body first, then removed it); (3) the CR/LF check from the .22 comment is done as a control-character check, with the real vectors tested (see below). TWO HOLES I FOUND IN MY OWN FIRST VERSION, each proved by a failing test before the fix: a content-type exemption for multipart let 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data' on a JSON route make FastAPI read an unbounded body (401/422 instead of 413: FastAPI calls request.body() whatever the type says), and an upload that declared 1 MiB and sent 300 was accepted (200) because only the declared length was checked. Both are closed by 'no exemption, one cap, lifted only by forward_upload, counting arrivals'. MEASURED on real processes (a fresh process per scenario, peak RSS growth over idle 59 MB; the 'before' sizes are smaller because the old code buffers about twice the body): BEFORE 250 MB authenticated proxy POST +508 MB; 200 MB unauthenticated JSON +607 MB (+806 MB chunked); 300 MB unauthenticated multipart taken in full before the 401; 300 MB authenticated upload +4 MB. AFTER 500 MB authenticated proxy POST +0 MB (413, 0 MB sent; chunked +0 MB, stops at the cap); 400 MB unauthenticated JSON +0 MB (413, 0 MB sent; chunked +0 MB); 300 MB authenticated upload +4 MB; 300 MB unauthenticated upload +1 MB, a 401, the app read none of it (uvicorn still drains the socket, no memory or disk). Aborted uploads: 8 aborted leave no open file and no temp file (in-process); see the floor note. ADVERSARY PASS, stated exactly: kit-adversary was asked at 18:44 with a brief naming the claims and 8 attack areas; it wrote 14 scripts under /tmp/adv-limits (t0 to t12) but sent NO written report in the hour that followed, despite a second ask. I therefore ran every one of its scripts myself against a real uvicorn (httptools and h11) and read the output, and re-ran the ones that exposed something after the fixes. I do not claim kit-adversary's sign-off. FIXED (db7eff5, each with a test that failed first): (a) t1: a zero-padded 5000-digit Content-Length that uvicorn's parser lets through made int() raise (4300-digit limit) and answered 500: declared_length strips zeros and treats 20+ digits as larger than any limit (now 200 for the padded 5, 413 for 9s); (b) t2/t3: a body that passes the cap while a response is already streaming (a GET stream whose server side listens on receive for the client to go) raised 413 after the response started: 'response already started' in the log and an abrupt end; the middleware now tracks the response and, past the limit while answering, reports the client as gone; (c) t4: the control check covered C0 and DEL only: now every Unicode control (C1 too) and line and paragraph separators, with ordinary names (Å, Ø, euro sign, curly quotes, CJK, emoji) tested to pass. HELD under attack (each tried by the scripts): duplicate and comma Content-Length (httptools 400; h11 takes identical ones, counted anyway), Content-Length plus Transfer-Encoding (h11 uses chunked: the arrival count stops it), negative, signed, hex, decimal and non-ASCII-digit lengths (400), Expect: 100-continue (401/403/413 are answered before any 100 is sent), pipelined requests after an early 413 or an unread 401 (the connection is closed, no desync), a keep-alive connection after a 413 (peer closed), chunk extensions and trailers, chunked exactly at the cap (200) and cap+1 (413), every method with a declared or chunked over-cap body (413), a mounted sub-app, a raw request.stream(), Request(scope, request.receive), the proxy, a File() route, WebSocket upgrade headers with a body, part-name spoofing (case, spaces, NUL, path), two file parts, text fields before or after the file, a filename with ; and quotes, a 40 MiB part header, a header block that never ends, a 20 MiB filename (400, +1 to +2 MiB RSS), a 3 MiB preamble (400), a security-headers check on the 413 (present). fds stay flat at 13 on the newest Starlette through aborted uploads, a 413 mid-stream, rejections after a 3 MiB parse, two-file 400s and Eneo down, on both HTTP parsers. RECORDED, NOT CHANGED (design.md): (1) memory at the cap: 50 concurrent valid 10 MiB bodies cost 13-26 MiB each (+813 MiB for request.body(), +915 to +1319 MiB for a JSON model), so a module public to the internet should set MAX_BODY_BYTES to its largest real JSON body; the cap bounds a request, not the sum of requests, and I did not build a global byte budget; (2) AT THE STARLETTE 1.3.1 FLOOR the temporary file of an upload cut off mid-way is closed at the next garbage collection, not at once (t10 at the floor: 13 open files at rest, 20 after 25 cut-offs, 25 after 75, 27 after 175, then steady; my in-process test missed it because it creates no reference cycles); Starlette 1.7.0 closes it at once (flat at 13). The clean fix is to raise the floor to starlette>=1.7.0; I did not, because that narrows compatibility and is the owner's call. (3) the file name is forwarded as it came, a path included (Eneo owns where a file lands). The 'multipart/form-data' ceiling uses a prefix match while Starlette's parser matches the exact type: a different-case or odd type that Starlette does not parse gets an empty form and a 400, tested. Docs: README (the upload example, MAX_BODY_BYTES, MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES), design K6/K7, plan Task 1.6 interface and changes. Exit checks on db7eff5 with fresh venvs: newest (fastapi 0.142.2, starlette 1.7.0, uvicorn 0.54.0, httpx2 2.13.1, httpcore2 2.13.1, python-multipart 0.0.32) 226 OK with -W error::DeprecationWarning; floors (starlette 1.3.1, httpx2 2.12.0, httpcore2 2.12.0, python-multipart 0.0.31) 226 OK; greps empty, no bare httpx; wheel built, installed in a fresh venv, 16 names, 226 OK against it; pip-audit clean on all three sets.

title: Phase 1.15 (P1): BFF hot path, throttle the session prune and compile the path scan
description:
Source: kit-perf review (P1 sessions, P2 path scan).

## Problem
1. SessionStore `get`/`create` scan every session under the lock on the event loop (auth.py ~162, 171): get 3 us @100 sessions, 28 us @1k, 311 us @10k, 3.5 ms @100k; a garbage cookie costs the same scan. Expired sessions (with tokens) stay in memory until some request arrives (1000 expired, 2 s idle: len 1000; 0 after one garbage-cookie get).
2. `leaves_route` (proxy.py ~120) loops per character in Python: 1.6 ms for a 16 KB path, 6.6 ms for 64 KB, per request.

## Required behaviour
- Prune expired sessions at most every 30 s (monotonic `_next_prune`); `get()` already rejects an expired id itself, so correctness does not depend on the prune. Prototype measured get 11 us / create 3 us @100k.
- `leaves_route`: one compiled `re.compile(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f\\]")` search over the path and over `unquote(path)`; behaviour identical, including every existing vector in the adversary tests (prototype 70 us / 305 us).
- Record, do not build: no session cap (each session needs an Eneo login, which Eneo rate-limits; a second login already ends the browser's old one) and no signed-URL single-flight (20 concurrent cold Range requests = 20 mints; low value). Add a one-line note for each in docs/design.md section 6 if not already covered.

## Tests first
Expiry still enforced between prunes (get of an expired id -> None without a prune); prune runs once per window (clock-injected); tokens of expired sessions are gone after the window; leaves_route vector table unchanged and a 64 KB path under a time bound.

## Acceptance
Numbers re-measured with the same scripts shape (get/create @10k, 64 KB path) and recorded in the close reason.

Tests first, shown failing on the old code: get 308 us at 10 000 sessions (bound 100 us), the sweep ran on every call (3 tests), leaves_route 5.9 ms / 9.0 ms / 8.4 ms on a 64 KB path (bound 2 ms). 210 tests green at the floors (starlette 1.3.1) and the newest (-W error::DeprecationWarning). 1 SESSION STORE: the scan of every session under the lock on every get and create is replaced by _prune_locked(), run at most every 30 s on the monotonic clock (_next_prune). get() refuses an expired id by itself and drops that id's session and signed URLs, so nothing depends on the sweep; tokens of expired sessions are gone one window later. Tests: expiry enforced between sweeps without a sweep (another expired session is still held), the sweep runs once per window (clock-injected, wall and monotonic together), expired sessions and their tokens are gone after the window, get/create bounded at 10 000 sessions (best of 7 under 100 us). The old test that relied on every call sweeping now advances the clock past the window; the FakeClock helper gained monotonic(). 2 leaves_route: the Python loops over every character and every segment are now two compiled searches ([\x00-\x1f\x7f\\] and the %XX that decodes to one, so nothing is decoded: a second decode has such a character exactly when the path has such a %XX) and a frozenset lookup over path.split('/') for the dot segments (the 12 spellings of . and .. with %2e/%2E). The bead's single combined pattern and its unquote(path) variant were measured and are slower (1 ms and 1.8 ms for 64 KB; see below). title: Phase 1.16 (P1): BFF streams, bounded pool wait, concurrent-stream cap, graceful shutdown
description:
Source: kit-perf review (P1 pool exhaustion, P2 shutdown).

## Problem
1. The shared client keeps httpx defaults (100 connections, pool timeout 60 s). 100 held Range streams: an ordinary proxy call answers 502 after 60.1-60.9 s and a new audio stream is 13 s late (app.py ~42-44).
2. uvicorn has no `timeout_graceful_shutdown` (serve.py): with open streams the BFF ignored SIGTERM for over 10 s, docker's default kill.
3. No total deadline anywhere (client 60 s per phase, upload 1800 s per read/write op).

## Required behaviour
- `httpx2.Timeout(60.0, connect=10.0, pool=5.0)` on the shared client; an `asyncio.Semaphore` (default 64, `Settings.max_concurrent_streams`) around `stream_signed`: when full, answer 503 with `Retry-After` immediately, leaving connections for the API.
- `serve()` sets `timeout_graceful_shutdown` below 10 s (suggest 8); prove SIGTERM with open streams exits in under 10 s.
- Item 3: record only (design note: per-phase timeouts are the contract; a total deadline is added when a module needs it). Do not build it now.

## Tests first
65th concurrent stream -> 503 + Retry-After while a proxy call to a fast fake Eneo still answers 200 in well under 5 s with 64 streams held; semaphore released when a client disconnects mid-stream (no leak after 200 aborted streams); SIGTERM test under open streams (subprocess, real uvicorn, wait on the process, no pkill).

## Acceptance
Measured: proxy latency with 64 held streams, and shutdown time with open streams, recorded in the close reason. Linux container re-run for the stream counts (macOS drops ~30% of 100 slow streams from kernel socket limits: not a BFF fault).
close_reason: Commit 5ed0482 on feat/bff (developed and measured in a scratch clone, cherry-picked unchanged). Tests first, shown failing on the old code: no stream_slots, no max_concurrent_streams, the pool timeout was 60 s (Timeout(60, connect=10) != pool=5), serve() had no timeout_graceful_shutdown. 221 tests green at the floors and the newest (-W error::DeprecationWarning), including the SIGTERM test against a real uvicorn in a subprocess. WHAT: stream_signed holds one of Settings.max_concurrent_streams (64, env MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS) slots (an asyncio.Semaphore on app.state.stream_slots) for as long as its file streams and answers 503 {error: streams_busy} with Retry-After: 2 at once when none is free, before it mints anything (a path that leaves its route is still a 403 first). The slot is given back by the response itself: _SlotStreamingResponse.__call__ releases it in a finally, shielded close of the upstream stream after, so a finished file, a client that went away (send raising OSError) and a cancelled request all free it; a stream that cannot start (mint refused, unreachable or unusable, file refused, redirected or unreachable) frees it at once. The shared client has Timeout(60, connect=10, pool=5). serve() sets timeout_graceful_shutdown=8 (GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_SECONDS), overridable. Recorded, not built: no total deadline (design.md section 6 and the README say per-phase timeouts are the contract). TESTS: 65th stream -> 503 + Retry-After while an API call still answers 200 (in-process, limit 3 and the real default of 64: 64 held, the 65th refused); the limit is checked before anything is minted; a slot is free again as soon as a stream ends (9 requests through 3 slots); a stream that cannot start takes no slot (6 failure modes plus a leaving-route 403); 200 streams cut off (100 by a failing send, 100 by cancellation) leave no slot taken, with no collection of garbage; settings default 64 and validation; pool=5 pinned; serve option pinned; SIGTERM with 5 open endless streams exits within 5 s with timeout_graceful_shutdown=1 (uvicorn re-raises the signal, so the status is 0 or -15). Mutation check: the release removed (3 tests fail), the release for a stream that cannot start removed (7 fail), pool back to 60 (1 fails), the shutdown option removed (3 fail); the mutant that removes the 503 check was not run because it blocks a request forever. MEASURED on a real module process (uvicorn, fake Eneo with an endless slow file, 100 streams attempted, macOS; same script before = the commit before this one): BEFORE all 100 streams admitted (200), then a proxy call answered 502 after 60.02 s, one more stream 502 after 60.01 s, and SIGTERM with the streams open did not stop the process within 40 s (killed by the script). AFTER 64 admitted and 36 refused 503 (slowest refusal 0.13 s), the proxy call 200 in 0.01 s, one more stream 503 in 0.00 s, SIGTERM with the streams open exits in 8.15 s (status -15, uvicorn re-raising the signal). REPEATED RUNS as the .24 comment asked, nothing retried away: the transport tests (which include the stream tests) 50 runs, 0 failures; the real-server scenario of 20 concurrent 64 MiB Range streams 30 runs on this code, 0 with a stream that was not 206 or was cut short (all 1280 MB delivered each time). The earlier one-off truncation did not recur. NOT DONE: a Linux container re-run of the stream counts (the bead asks for one; macOS can drop slow connections from kernel socket limits, but all 100 attempts here were answered, 64 + 36, so no connection was lost on this run); there is no container in this session.
